messages:
Maria (eng-ml): Pushed a short perf microtrace for a handful of tenant samples — saw repeated token-latency spikes that line up with kernel fallbacks + KV miss storms. trace: https://perf.redwood/trace/17845 :eyes:
Ajay (eng-runtime): Nice, can you paste the PromQL or the query you used for the token-level breakdown? want to see the buckets you used.
Maria (eng-ml): PromQL snippet I used (very rough):
```
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(token_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, kernel, route, org_id))
```
That gave p95 per-token split by kernel+org. the weird bit is a tiny set of orgs where p50 is fine but p95 >> p99 of others.
Lia (product): If it's just a few workspaces, we need an RBAC-friendly dashboard view for customer support. Can we expose a per-workspace KPI with masked org ids?
Devon (eng-platform): We should avoid unbounded label cardinality. plan: keep org_id as a coarse bucket (org_tier/region) by default, and allow sampled detailed traces for support-only scopes. sampling policy: 0.5% baseline + on-demand for support.
Samir (eng-sre): Cardinality + retention are my worry too. If you tag every token with org_id+kernel+route you'll kill storage. Suggest aggregate per-route token histograms plus a small table of sampled microtraces. Also set a TTL of 7d for per-org microtraces.
Ajay (eng-runtime): On the runtime side I can add a `kernel_path` label to the microtrace (values: optimized, fallback, quantized) and emit KV hit/miss counters keyed by `org_shard` (coarse). That lets us correlate kernel switch -> KV miss storm -> latency.
Maria (eng-ml): here's a tiny example of the header we attach in requests for scoping: `X-Workspace-ID: ws_12345` — implementation would map to `org_shard: ws_1` before metrics emission so we don't explode cardinality.
Devon (eng-platform): For dashboards I'd like these panels: p50/p95/p99 token latency (per-route), cache hit ratio over time (org_shard), kernel-fallback rate, and a Sankey that shows traffic flow from route -> kernel -> cache result -> latency bucket. Sankey is great to spot hot paths.
Lia (product): For support RBAC, proposal: console shows coarse org-tier metrics by default; support role can opt into sampled deep traces for a specific tenant for 1 hour. All exports redact PII.
Samir (eng-sre): Also add alerts: if kernel-fallback-rate > 2% for >5m AND cache-miss-rate > 1k/min for a shard, open a ticket. Keep thresholds adaptive per-tenant traffic.
Ajay (eng-runtime): Implementation note: sampling should be decided at edge (ingress) so we tag the request with `trace_sample=1` early then propagate. Avoid sampling after kernel fallback or we'll bias.
Maria (eng-ml): Agreed. Also recorded a small perf regression timeline in the doc: https://docs.redwood/internal/tenant-perf-regressions — looks like a quantization kernel change two weeks ago lines up.
Devon (eng-platform): Next steps:
- Ajay: add `kernel_path` + `org_shard` labels, KV hit/miss counters (ETA 3d)
- Maria: push dashboard mockups (Sankey + per-route panels) and example queries (ETA 2d)
- Samir: draft retention & alert thresholds (ETA 1d)
Lia (product): I'll draft RBAC UX for console access to sampled traces.
metrics-bot: Alert created: `tenant-kernel-fallback-spike` -> https://alerts.redwood/1784501234 (auto-generated) :bell:
Maria (eng-ml): Thanks all — I'll upload the sampled trace exports to the shared perf bucket and tag the example tenants. ping me if you want a live walkthrough later today. :thumbsup:
